docs.title: Festo Gripper
docs.text: festo-dev-gripper is a Python library providing a reference implementation of controls for a digital-IO-based Festo parallel gripper using the festo-cpx-io library.

docs.title: From Codebase
docs.text:
Navigate to the directory where the code is stored and, using uv, type in the following command:

uv pip install -e .

This will package the library locally and can be used as regular imports.

docs.title: Official Packaged Releases
docs.text:
The latest released version of this package can be found on the package registry of this project. Install using uv:

uv add festo-dev-gripper

docs.title: From Git Repository
docs.text:
uv pip install git+https://github.com/Festo-se/festo-dev-gripper.git

Or as an editable dependency with a local copy of the source code:

  1. Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/Festo-se/festo-dev-gripper.git <destination-directory>
  1. Navigate to the clone destination directory
cd <destination>
  1. Install with uv
uv pip install -e .

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text: festo-dev-gripper depends on festo-cpx-io for communicating with the Festo CPX I/O system.

docs.title: Basic CPX-E gripper
docs.text:
examples/gripper_demo.py loads controller and module classes from Spec 3.0 configuration. It does not hard-code CpxE, CpxE16Di, CpxE8Do, or CpxEEp imports.

Run only with safe hardware connected:

GRIPPER_CPX_IP=192.168.0.41 python examples/gripper_demo.py

Core pattern:

import os
from importlib import import_module
from pathlib import Path

from gripper.config_adapter import load_config
from gripper.gripper import Gripper

config = load_config(Path("src/gripper/data/gripper-config.json"))
controller = config["components"]["controller"]
package = ".".join(
    (
        controller["control_library"],
        controller["control_system"],
        controller["control_bus"],
    )
)

module_name, class_name = next(iter(controller["control_module"].items()))
controller_class = getattr(import_module(f"{package}.{module_name}"), class_name)
modules = []
for module_spec in controller["modules"]:
    module_name, class_name = next(iter(module_spec.items()))
    module_class = getattr(import_module(f"{package}.{module_name}"), class_name)
    modules.append(module_class())

control_class = controller_class
control = control_class(
    ip_address=os.getenv("GRIPPER_CPX_IP", controller["ip"]),
    modules=modules,
)
gripper = Gripper(control, config)

try:
    gripper.release()
    print(gripper.get_status().get_position())
    gripper.grip()
    print(gripper.get_status().get_position())
finally:
    control.shutdown()

Configuration selects output and sensor modules:

"control_signal_module": {"e8do": "CpxE8Do"},
"control_signal_channels": {"grip": 1, "release": 0},
"sensor": {
  "control_signal_module": {"e16di": "CpxE16Di"},
  "control_signal_channels": {"grip": 0, "release": 1}
}

CpxE8Do drives outputs. CpxE16Di reads closed/gripping input on channel 0 and open/released input on channel 1.

docs.title: Gripper
docs.text:
Gripper control class for CPX-based gripping modules.

control is dependency-injected. It must expose write_channel and reset_channel. Sensor-enabled controls must also expose either sensor_module or a modules iterable containing configured sensors via digital input. Constructor does not create or close hardware resources.

Source code in src/gripper/gripper.py 
class Gripper:
    """Gripper control class for CPX-based gripping modules.

    ``control`` is dependency-injected. It must expose ``write_channel`` and
    ``reset_channel``. Sensor-enabled controls must also expose either
    ``sensor_module`` or a ``modules`` iterable containing configured
    ``sensors via digital input``. Constructor does not create or close hardware resources.
    """

    def __init__(self, control, config: dict, component_name: str | None = None, sensor_control=None):
        """Initialize gripper from normalized legacy-compatible config.

        Args:
            control: Injected CPX control assembly.
            config: Mapping with ``components.gripper`` and
                ``control_signal_channels``. Optional ``sensor`` config maps
                CPX-E16DI channels 0 and 1 to gripping and release states.
            component_name: Name of gripper component in config, used when multiple grippers are present.
            sensor_control: Optional controller assembly used for sensor module lookup.

        Raises:
            KeyError: Required configuration field is absent.
            ValueError: Configured sensor module cannot be found.
        """
        logger.debug("Gripper initialization started")
        self.control = control
        components = config["components"]
        self.config = components.get("gripper", components.get(component_name))
        if self.config is None and control is None:
            raise KeyError("No instantiated control or valid config given.")
        self.channels_config = self.config["control_signal_channels"]
        self.grip_channel = self.channels_config["grip"]
        self.release_channel = self.channels_config["release"]
        if self.grip_channel == self.release_channel:
            raise ValueError("grip and release channels must be distinct")
        self._owned_control = None
        self._sensor_control = sensor_control
        self.sensor = self._build_sensor(self._sensor_control)
        logger.info(
            "Gripper initialized: grip_channel=%s release_channel=%s sensor=%s",
            self.grip_channel,
            self.release_channel,
            self.sensor is not None,
        )

    @classmethod
    def from_config(cls, source, component_name: str | None = None, ip_address: str | None = None):
        """Construct gripper and CPX modules from Spec 3.0 configuration."""
        ## TODO: AP module has autorecognition, so explicit IOs are not clear except from some kind of info or other config. Need this to bootstrap and understand system topology of actuators, sensors, etc.
        # TODO: COnfig options: AP still positional in terms of IO modules, this is how the config shuold be structured, avoid hardcoding indices for controls
        # TODO: Map :  cpx.module[index].set_channel(other index) -> human understandable methods/verbs

        adapter = GripperConfigAdapter(source, component_name=component_name)
        config = adapter.get_gripper_config()
        controller = config["components"]["controller"]
        package = ".".join((controller["control_library"], controller["control_system"], controller["control_bus"]))
        selected = config["components"]["gripper"]
        try:
            module_specs = controller["modules"]
            modules = [cls._instantiate_module(package, spec) for spec in module_specs]
            controller_spec = controller["control_module"]
            controller_module, controller_class = cls._single_mapping(controller_spec, "control_module")
            controller_type = getattr(import_module(f"{package}.{controller_module}"), controller_class)
            address = ip_address or os.getenv("GRIPPER_CPX_IP") or controller.get("ip", "192.168.0.2")
            base = controller_type(ip_address=address, modules=modules)
            output_name, output_class = cls._single_mapping(
                selected.get("control_signal_module", {}), "control_signal_module"
            )
            output = next(
                (
                    module
                    for module in base.modules
                    if type(module).__name__ == output_class or getattr(module, "name", None) == output_name
                ),
                None,
            )
            if output is None:
                raise GripperFactoryError(f"Configured output module not found: {output_class}")
            result = cls(output, config, component_name=component_name, sensor_control=base)
            result._owned_control = base
            return result
        except Exception as exc:
            if "base" in locals() and hasattr(base, "shutdown"):
                base.shutdown()
            if isinstance(exc, (ConfigValidationError, GripperFactoryError, ValueError, KeyError)):
                raise
            raise GripperFactoryError(f"Unable to construct configured gripper: {exc}") from exc

    @staticmethod
    def _single_mapping(value, field):
        if not isinstance(value, dict) or len(value) != 1:
            raise ValueError(f"{field} must contain exactly one item")
        return next(iter(value.items()))

    @classmethod
    def _instantiate_module(cls, package, spec):
        name, class_name = cls._single_mapping(spec, "module")
        module_type = getattr(import_module(f"{package}.{name}"), class_name)
        return module_type()

    def close(self):
        """Shut down CPX control when factory created it."""
        if self._owned_control is not None:
            control, self._owned_control = self._owned_control, None
            control.shutdown()

    def __enter__(self):
        """Return factory-owned gripper for context management."""
        return self

    def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc_value, traceback):
        """Close factory-owned CPX control after context exit."""
        self.close()

    def _wait(self, timeout: int):
        """Wait ``timeout`` polling cycles.

        Each cycle sleeps for 10 ms. Existing synchronous timing behavior is
        preserved; argument is cycle count, not elapsed milliseconds.
        """
        logger.debug("Gripper wait started: cycles=%s interval_seconds=0.01", timeout)
        for _ in range(timeout):
            # self.control.read_channel(self.channel_numbers[0]) # why?
            time.sleep(0.01)
        logger.debug("Gripper wait completed: cycles=%s", timeout)

    def _set_gripper(self, to_open: bool):
        """Pulse mutually exclusive outputs to open or close gripper.

        Args:
            to_open: ``True`` energizes release output; ``False`` energizes grip.

        Both outputs are reset in ``finally`` after command starts, including
        hardware write, wait, or reset failures.
        """
        logger.info("Gripper output command started: to_open=%s", to_open)
        self._wait(15)
        try:
            self.control.write_channel(self.release_channel, to_open)
            self.control.write_channel(self.grip_channel, not to_open)
            logger.debug(
                "Gripper outputs written: release_channel=%s release_value=%s grip_channel=%s grip_value=%s",
                self.release_channel,
                to_open,
                self.grip_channel,
                not to_open,
            )
            self._wait(100)
            logger.info("Gripper output command completed: to_open=%s", to_open)
        except Exception:
            logger.exception("Gripper output command failed: to_open=%s", to_open)
            raise
        finally:
            try:
                self.control.reset_channel(self.release_channel)
                self.control.reset_channel(self.grip_channel)
            except Exception:
                logger.exception("Gripper output reset failed")
                raise
            logger.debug("Gripper outputs reset")

    def _build_sensor(self, control):
        """Resolve configured digital-input module and create sensor reader."""
        logger.debug("Gripper sensor construction started")
        sensor_config = self.config.get("sensor")
        if not sensor_config:
            return None
        module_spec = sensor_config.get("control_signal_module")
        if not isinstance(module_spec, dict) or len(module_spec) != 1:
            raise ValueError("Sensor control_signal_module must contain exactly one module")
        module_name, module_class = next(iter(module_spec.items()))
        module = getattr(control, "sensor_module", None)
        for candidate in getattr(control, "modules", []):
            if type(candidate).__name__ == module_class or getattr(candidate, "name", None) == module_name:
                module = candidate
                break
        if module is None:
            raise ValueError(f"Configured sensor module not found: {module_class}")
        return GripperSensor(module, sensor_config["control_signal_channels"])

    def check_sensor_status(self) -> GripperStatus:
        """Read configured inputs and classify gripper state."""
        if self.sensor is None:
            return GripperStatus(0)
        readings = self.sensor.read()
        if readings["grip"] and readings["release"]:
            return GripperStatus(2, "fault", "unknown", "contradictory")
        if readings["grip"]:
            return GripperStatus(0, "gripping", "stopped", "closed")
        if readings["release"]:
            return GripperStatus(0, "released", "stopped", "open")
        return GripperStatus(1, "unknown", "moving", None)

    def get_status(self) -> GripperStatus:
        """Return current status from configured position sensors."""
        return self.check_sensor_status()

    def grip(self):
        """Command gripper to enter grip state using configured grip output pulse."""
        logger.info("Gripper grip requested")
        self._set_gripper(to_open=False)
        self._wait(1)
        logger.info("Gripper grip completed")

    def release(self):
        """Release gripper from "grip" state using configured release output pulse."""
        logger.info("Gripper release requested")
        self._set_gripper(to_open=True)
        self._wait(1)
        logger.info("Gripper release completed")

docs.title: GripperSensor
docs.text:
Read open and closed gripper switches from a digital-input module.

channels["grip"] identifies closed/gripping input. channels["release"] identifies open/released input. Sensor values are normalized to bool; hardware-specific input classes stay behind module.

Source code in src/gripper/gripper.py 
class GripperSensor:
    """Read open and closed gripper switches from a digital-input module.

    ``channels["grip"]`` identifies closed/gripping input. ``channels["release"]``
    identifies open/released input. Sensor values are normalized to ``bool``;
    hardware-specific input classes stay behind ``module``.
    """

    def __init__(self, module, channels: dict):
        """Create sensor reader.

        Args:
            module: Digital-input module exposing ``read_channel(channel)``.
            channels: Mapping containing integer ``grip`` and ``release`` channels.
        """
        logger.debug("GripperSensor initialization started")
        self.module = module
        self.grip_channel = channels["grip"]
        self.release_channel = channels["release"]
        logger.debug(
            "GripperSensor initialized: grip_channel=%s release_channel=%s",
            self.grip_channel,
            self.release_channel,
        )

    def read(self) -> dict[str, bool]:
        """Read both configured inputs and map them to semantic states.

        Returns:
            Dictionary with ``grip`` and ``release`` boolean readings.

        Raises:
            Exception: Propagates hardware read failures unchanged.
        """
        logger.debug("GripperSensor read started")
        try:
            readings = {
                "grip": bool(self.module.read_channel(self.grip_channel)),
                "release": bool(self.module.read_channel(self.release_channel)),
            }
        except Exception:
            logger.exception("GripperSensor read failed")
            raise
        logger.debug("Gripper sensor readings: %s", readings)
        return readings

docs.text:
Snapshot of gripper position, motion, and fault state.

code uses 0 for a valid state, 1 for indeterminate inputs, and 2 for contradictory sensor inputs. State strings remain available through accessors for callers that do not want to interpret numeric codes.

Source code in src/gripper/gripper.py 
class GripperStatus:
    """Snapshot of gripper position, motion, and fault state.

    ``code`` uses ``0`` for a valid state, ``1`` for indeterminate inputs,
    and ``2`` for contradictory sensor inputs. State strings remain available
    through accessors for callers that do not want to interpret numeric codes.
    """

    def __init__(self, code, gripping_state="unknown", movement_state="unknown", position=None):
        """Create status snapshot.

        Args:
            code: Numeric status code: 0 valid, 1 unknown, 2 fault.
            gripping_state: Semantic gripping state.
            movement_state: Semantic movement state.
            position: ``"gripped"``, ``"released"``, ``"contradictory"``, or ``None``.
        """
        logger.debug(
            "GripperStatus created: code=%s gripping_state=%s movement_state=%s position=%s",
            code,
            gripping_state,
            movement_state,
            position,
        )
        self.code = code
        self.gripping_state = gripping_state
        self.movement_state = movement_state
        self.position = position

    def get_gripping_state(self):
        """Return semantic gripping state."""
        logger.debug("GripperStatus gripping state requested: state=%s", self.gripping_state)
        return self.gripping_state

    def get_movement_state(self):
        """Return semantic movement state."""
        logger.debug("GripperStatus movement state requested: state=%s", self.movement_state)
        return self.movement_state

    def get_position(self):
        """Return semantic position, or ``None`` when unavailable."""
        logger.debug("GripperStatus position requested: position=%s", self.position)
        return self.position

class GripperConfigAdapter:
    """
    Translate between old Python dict format and new spec 3.0 JSON schema.

    Handles both formats transparently:
    - Old format: Python dict (legacy test_config.py)
    - New format: Spec 3.0 JSON with component_spec_version 2.0

    Adapter detects format at load time and translates new → old field names
    internally, so old code sees identical dict structure. Deprecation warnings
    guide users to new schema.
    """

    OLD_FORMAT_VERSION = "1.0"
    NEW_FORMAT_VERSION = "3.0"
    COMPONENT_SPEC_VERSION = "2.0"

    def __init__(self, config: Union[Dict[str, Any], str, Path], component_name: str | None = None) -> None:
        """
        Load config from dict, JSON file, or path string.

        Args:
            config: Config dict, file path (str/Path), or JSON content string
            component_name: Optional named gripper component selector

        Raises:
            ConfigValidationError: Schema validation fails
        """
        logger.debug("GripperConfigAdapter initialization started: config_type=%s", type(config).__name__)
        if isinstance(config, (str, Path)):
            logger.debug("Loading gripper config file: path=%s", config)
            config = self._load_json_file(config)

        self.raw_config = config
        self.component_name = component_name
        self.is_new_schema = self._detect_schema_version()
        logger.debug("Detected gripper config schema: new=%s", self.is_new_schema)

        if self.is_new_schema:
            self._validate_spec_3_0()
            self.config = self._translate_spec_3_0_to_legacy()
            logger.info("Translated spec 3.0 gripper config to legacy format")
            logger.warning(
                "Spec 3.0 config detected. Migration path available: See docs/MIGRATION.md for upgrade guide."
            )
        else:
            self._validate_legacy()
            self.config = config
            logger.debug("Legacy config loaded (old Python dict format)")
        logger.debug("GripperConfigAdapter initialization completed: new_schema=%s", self.is_new_schema)

    def get_gripper_config(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Return normalized config dict compatible with Gripper."""
        logger.debug("Normalized gripper config requested")
        return self.config

    @staticmethod
    def _load_json_file(path: Union[str, Path]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Load and parse JSON file."""
        logger.debug("JSON gripper config load started: path=%s", path)
        path = Path(path)
        if not path.exists():
            logger.error("Gripper config file not found: path=%s", path)
            raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config file not found: {path}")
        try:
            with open(path, "r") as f:
                config = json.load(f)
                logger.debug("Gripper config file loaded: path=%s", path)
                return config
        except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
            logger.error("Invalid gripper config JSON: path=%s", path)
            raise ConfigValidationError(f"Invalid JSON in {path}: {e}") from e

    def _detect_schema_version(self) -> bool:
        """Detect if config is new spec 3.0 (True) or old format (False)."""
        # New schema has spec_version key at top level
        detected = "spec_version" in self.raw_config
        logger.debug("Gripper config schema detection completed: new_schema=%s", detected)
        return detected

    def _validate_legacy(self) -> None:
        """Validate old Python dict format."""
        logger.debug("Legacy gripper config validation started")
        required_paths = [
            ("components",),
            ("components", "gripper"),
            ("components", "gripper", "control_signal_channels"),
            ("components", "gripper", "control_signal_channels", "grip"),
            ("components", "gripper", "control_signal_channels", "release"),
        ]

        for path in required_paths:
            try:
                self._get_nested(self.raw_config, path)
            except KeyError:
                logger.error("Legacy gripper config missing field: path=%s", ".".join(path))
                raise ConfigValidationError(f"Missing required field in legacy config: {'.'.join(path)}") from None

        # Validate channel types
        grip = self._get_nested(self.raw_config, ("components", "gripper", "control_signal_channels", "grip"))
        release = self._get_nested(self.raw_config, ("components", "gripper", "control_signal_channels", "release"))

        if not isinstance(grip, int):
            logger.error("Legacy gripper grip channel has invalid type: type=%s", type(grip).__name__)
            raise ConfigValidationError(f"grip channel must be int, got {type(grip).__name__}")
        if not isinstance(release, int):
            logger.error("Legacy gripper release channel has invalid type: type=%s", type(release).__name__)
            raise ConfigValidationError(f"release channel must be int, got {type(release).__name__}")
        logger.debug("Legacy gripper config validation completed")

    def _validate_spec_3_0(self) -> None:
        """Validate spec 3.0 schema structure."""
        logger.debug("Spec 3.0 gripper config validation started")
        required_top_level = ("spec_version", "component_config")
        for field in required_top_level:
            if field not in self.raw_config:
                logger.error("Spec 3.0 gripper config missing top-level field: field=%s", field)
                raise ConfigValidationError(f"Missing required top-level field: {field}")

        if self.raw_config["spec_version"] != self.NEW_FORMAT_VERSION:
            logger.error("Unsupported gripper config schema: version=%s", self.raw_config["spec_version"])
            raise ConfigValidationError(
                f"Unsupported spec_version: {self.raw_config['spec_version']}. Expected {self.NEW_FORMAT_VERSION}"
            )

        # Validate component structure
        components = self._get_nested(self.raw_config, ("component_config", "components"))
        if not isinstance(components, dict):
            logger.error("Spec 3.0 gripper components are not a dict")
            raise ConfigValidationError("component_config.components must be a dict")

        gripper_config = self._select_gripper_component(components)

        if not gripper_config:
            logger.error("Spec 3.0 gripper component not found")
            raise ConfigValidationError("No component with component_class='gripper' found")

        # Validate required gripper fields
        required_gripper_fields = (
            "component_spec_version",
            "control_signal_channels",
        )
        for field in required_gripper_fields:
            if field not in gripper_config:
                logger.error("Spec 3.0 gripper component missing field: field=%s", field)
                raise ConfigValidationError(f"Gripper component missing required field: {field}")

        # Validate signal channels
        channels = gripper_config["control_signal_channels"]
        self._validate_signal_channels(channels)
        self._validate_component_mappings(gripper_config)
        logger.debug("Spec 3.0 gripper config validation completed")

    def _validate_signal_channels(self, channels: Any) -> None:
        logger.debug("Gripper control signal channel validation started")
        if not isinstance(channels, dict):
            logger.error("Gripper control signal channels are not a dict")
            raise ConfigValidationError("control_signal_channels must be a dict")
        if "grip" not in channels or "release" not in channels:
            logger.error("Gripper control signal channels missing grip or release")
            raise ConfigValidationError("control_signal_channels must have 'grip' and 'release' keys")
        if type(channels["grip"]) is not int or type(channels["release"]) is not int:
            logger.error("Gripper control signal channels have invalid types")
            raise ConfigValidationError("grip/release channels must be integers")
        if channels["grip"] == channels["release"]:
            raise ConfigValidationError("grip and release channels must be distinct")
        logger.debug("Gripper control signal channel validation completed")

    def _validate_component_mappings(self, gripper_config: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        """Validate dynamic-import metadata without importing any hardware code."""
        output = gripper_config.get("control_signal_module")
        if output is not None:
            self._validate_single_mapping(output, "control_signal_module")

        control_modules = gripper_config.get("control_modules")
        if control_modules is None:
            return
        if not isinstance(control_modules, dict) or not isinstance(control_modules.get("controller"), dict):
            raise ConfigValidationError("Gripper control_modules.controller must be a mapping")
        controller = control_modules["controller"]
        for field in ("control_library", "control_system", "control_bus", "ip"):
            if field in controller and not isinstance(controller[field], str):
                raise ConfigValidationError(f"controller.{field} must be a string")
        if "control_module" in controller:
            self._validate_single_mapping(controller["control_module"], "control_module")
        if "controller" in controller:
            self._validate_single_mapping(controller["controller"], "controller")
        modules = controller.get("modules")
        if modules is not None and not isinstance(modules, list):
            raise ConfigValidationError("controller.modules must be a list")
        for module in modules or []:
            self._validate_single_mapping(module, "controller.modules item")

    @staticmethod
    def _validate_single_mapping(value: Any, field: str) -> None:
        if not isinstance(value, dict) or len(value) != 1:
            raise ConfigValidationError(f"{field} must contain exactly one item")

    def _translate_spec_3_0_to_legacy(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Translate spec 3.0 config to old Python dict format."""
        logger.debug("Spec 3.0 gripper config translation started")
        # Extract gripper component
        components = self._get_nested(self.raw_config, ("component_config", "components"))
        gripper_config = None

        gripper_config = self._select_gripper_component(components)

        if not gripper_config:
            logger.error("Spec 3.0 gripper component missing during translation")
            raise ConfigValidationError("No gripper component found in spec 3.0 config")

        # Build legacy format
        translated = {
            "components": {
                "gripper": {
                    "control_signal_channels": gripper_config["control_signal_channels"],
                    "control_signal_module": gripper_config.get("control_signal_module", {}),
                    "sensor": gripper_config.get("sensor"),
                    # Preserve other fields if present
                    "uuid": gripper_config.get("uuid", "0000-000000000-000000-000"),
                    "type": gripper_config.get("type", "parallel"),
                    "control_signal": gripper_config.get("control_signal", "digital"),
                },
                # Include controller if present (from control_modules)
                "controller": self._extract_controller_config(gripper_config),
            }
        }
        logger.debug("Spec 3.0 gripper config translation completed")
        return translated

    def _select_gripper_component(self, components: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Select one named gripper, or the sole gripper when unnamed."""
        grippers = {
            name: spec
            for name, spec in components.items()
            if isinstance(spec, dict) and spec.get("component_class") == "gripper"
        }
        if self.component_name is not None:
            if self.component_name not in grippers:
                raise ConfigValidationError(f"Unknown gripper component: {self.component_name}")
            return grippers[self.component_name]
        if not grippers:
            raise ConfigValidationError("No component with component_class='gripper' found")
        if len(grippers) != 1:
            raise ConfigValidationError(
                f"Gripper component selector is required when config contains {len(grippers)} gripper components"
            )
        return next(iter(grippers.values()))

    @staticmethod
    def _extract_controller_config(gripper_config: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Extract controller config from gripper's control_modules."""
        logger.debug("Controller config extraction started")
        control_modules = gripper_config.get("control_modules", {})
        controller = control_modules.get("controller", {})
        control_system = controller.get("control_system", "cpx_system")
        control_bus = controller.get("control_bus")
        if control_bus is None and "." in control_system:
            control_system, control_bus = control_system.split(".", 1)

        # Return controller with defaults if not present
        controller_config = {
            "control_library": controller.get("control_library", "cpx_io"),
            "control_system": control_system,
            "control_bus": control_bus or "cpx_e",
            "control_module": controller.get("control_module", {"cpx_e": "CpxE"}),
            "controller": controller.get("controller", {"eep": "CpxEEp"}),
            "ip": controller.get("ip", "192.168.0.41"),
            "modules": controller.get("modules", []),
        }
        logger.debug("Controller config extraction completed: module_count=%s", len(controller_config["modules"]))
        return controller_config

    @staticmethod
    def _get_nested(d: Dict[str, Any], path: tuple) -> Any:
        """Get nested dict value by path tuple."""
        logger.debug("Nested gripper config value requested: path=%s", ".".join(path))
        result = d
        for key in path:
            result = result[key]
        logger.debug("Nested gripper config value found: path=%s", ".".join(path))
        return result

def load_config(config_path: Union[str, Path], component_name: str | None = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Load config file (spec 3.0 or legacy) and return normalized dict.

    Handles migration transparently. Logs deprecation warning if legacy format.

        component_name: Optional named gripper component selector

    logger.info("Gripper config load completed: new_schema=%s", adapter.is_new_schema)
    return config

class Gripper:
    """Gripper control class for CPX-based gripping modules.

    ``control`` is dependency-injected. It must expose ``write_channel`` and
    ``reset_channel``. Sensor-enabled controls must also expose either
    ``sensor_module`` or a ``modules`` iterable containing configured
    ``sensors via digital input``. Constructor does not create or close hardware resources.
    """

    def __init__(self, control, config: dict, component_name: str | None = None, sensor_control=None):
        """Initialize gripper from normalized legacy-compatible config.

        Args:
            control: Injected CPX control assembly.
            config: Mapping with ``components.gripper`` and
                ``control_signal_channels``. Optional ``sensor`` config maps
                CPX-E16DI channels 0 and 1 to gripping and release states.
            component_name: Name of gripper component in config, used when multiple grippers are present.
            sensor_control: Optional controller assembly used for sensor module lookup.

        Raises:
            KeyError: Required configuration field is absent.
            ValueError: Configured sensor module cannot be found.
        """
        logger.debug("Gripper initialization started")
        self.control = control
        components = config["components"]
        self.config = components.get("gripper", components.get(component_name))
        if self.config is None and control is None:
            raise KeyError("No instantiated control or valid config given.")
        self.channels_config = self.config["control_signal_channels"]
        self.grip_channel = self.channels_config["grip"]
        self.release_channel = self.channels_config["release"]
        if self.grip_channel == self.release_channel:
            raise ValueError("grip and release channels must be distinct")
        self._owned_control = None
        self._sensor_control = sensor_control
        self.sensor = self._build_sensor(self._sensor_control)
        logger.info(
            "Gripper initialized: grip_channel=%s release_channel=%s sensor=%s",
            self.grip_channel,
            self.release_channel,
            self.sensor is not None,
        )

    @classmethod
    def from_config(cls, source, component_name: str | None = None, ip_address: str | None = None):
        """Construct gripper and CPX modules from Spec 3.0 configuration."""
        ## TODO: AP module has autorecognition, so explicit IOs are not clear except from some kind of info or other config. Need this to bootstrap and understand system topology of actuators, sensors, etc.
        # TODO: COnfig options: AP still positional in terms of IO modules, this is how the config shuold be structured, avoid hardcoding indices for controls
        # TODO: Map :  cpx.module[index].set_channel(other index) -> human understandable methods/verbs

        adapter = GripperConfigAdapter(source, component_name=component_name)
        config = adapter.get_gripper_config()
        controller = config["components"]["controller"]
        package = ".".join((controller["control_library"], controller["control_system"], controller["control_bus"]))
        selected = config["components"]["gripper"]
        try:
            module_specs = controller["modules"]
            modules = [cls._instantiate_module(package, spec) for spec in module_specs]
            controller_spec = controller["control_module"]
            controller_module, controller_class = cls._single_mapping(controller_spec, "control_module")
            controller_type = getattr(import_module(f"{package}.{controller_module}"), controller_class)
            address = ip_address or os.getenv("GRIPPER_CPX_IP") or controller.get("ip", "192.168.0.2")
            base = controller_type(ip_address=address, modules=modules)
            output_name, output_class = cls._single_mapping(
                selected.get("control_signal_module", {}), "control_signal_module"
            )
            output = next(
                (
                    module
                    for module in base.modules
                    if type(module).__name__ == output_class or getattr(module, "name", None) == output_name
                ),
                None,
            )
            if output is None:
                raise GripperFactoryError(f"Configured output module not found: {output_class}")
            result = cls(output, config, component_name=component_name, sensor_control=base)
            result._owned_control = base
            return result
        except Exception as exc:
            if "base" in locals() and hasattr(base, "shutdown"):
                base.shutdown()
            if isinstance(exc, (ConfigValidationError, GripperFactoryError, ValueError, KeyError)):
                raise
            raise GripperFactoryError(f"Unable to construct configured gripper: {exc}") from exc

    @staticmethod
    def _single_mapping(value, field):
        if not isinstance(value, dict) or len(value) != 1:
            raise ValueError(f"{field} must contain exactly one item")
        return next(iter(value.items()))

    @classmethod
    def _instantiate_module(cls, package, spec):
        name, class_name = cls._single_mapping(spec, "module")
        module_type = getattr(import_module(f"{package}.{name}"), class_name)
        return module_type()

    def close(self):
        """Shut down CPX control when factory created it."""
        if self._owned_control is not None:
            control, self._owned_control = self._owned_control, None
            control.shutdown()

    def __enter__(self):
        """Return factory-owned gripper for context management."""
        return self

    def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc_value, traceback):
        """Close factory-owned CPX control after context exit."""
        self.close()

    def _wait(self, timeout: int):
        """Wait ``timeout`` polling cycles.

        Each cycle sleeps for 10 ms. Existing synchronous timing behavior is
        preserved; argument is cycle count, not elapsed milliseconds.
        """
        logger.debug("Gripper wait started: cycles=%s interval_seconds=0.01", timeout)
        for _ in range(timeout):
            # self.control.read_channel(self.channel_numbers[0]) # why?
            time.sleep(0.01)
        logger.debug("Gripper wait completed: cycles=%s", timeout)

    def _set_gripper(self, to_open: bool):
        """Pulse mutually exclusive outputs to open or close gripper.

        Args:
            to_open: ``True`` energizes release output; ``False`` energizes grip.

        Both outputs are reset in ``finally`` after command starts, including
        hardware write, wait, or reset failures.
        """
        logger.info("Gripper output command started: to_open=%s", to_open)
        self._wait(15)
        try:
            self.control.write_channel(self.release_channel, to_open)
            self.control.write_channel(self.grip_channel, not to_open)
            logger.debug(
                "Gripper outputs written: release_channel=%s release_value=%s grip_channel=%s grip_value=%s",
                self.release_channel,
                to_open,
                self.grip_channel,
                not to_open,
            )
            self._wait(100)
            logger.info("Gripper output command completed: to_open=%s", to_open)
        except Exception:
            logger.exception("Gripper output command failed: to_open=%s", to_open)
            raise
        finally:
            try:
                self.control.reset_channel(self.release_channel)
                self.control.reset_channel(self.grip_channel)
            except Exception:
                logger.exception("Gripper output reset failed")
                raise
            logger.debug("Gripper outputs reset")

    def _build_sensor(self, control):
        """Resolve configured digital-input module and create sensor reader."""
        logger.debug("Gripper sensor construction started")
        sensor_config = self.config.get("sensor")
        if not sensor_config:
            return None
        module_spec = sensor_config.get("control_signal_module")
        if not isinstance(module_spec, dict) or len(module_spec) != 1:
            raise ValueError("Sensor control_signal_module must contain exactly one module")
        module_name, module_class = next(iter(module_spec.items()))
        module = getattr(control, "sensor_module", None)
        for candidate in getattr(control, "modules", []):
            if type(candidate).__name__ == module_class or getattr(candidate, "name", None) == module_name:
                module = candidate
                break
        if module is None:
            raise ValueError(f"Configured sensor module not found: {module_class}")
        return GripperSensor(module, sensor_config["control_signal_channels"])

    def check_sensor_status(self) -> GripperStatus:
        """Read configured inputs and classify gripper state."""
        if self.sensor is None:
            return GripperStatus(0)
        readings = self.sensor.read()
        if readings["grip"] and readings["release"]:
            return GripperStatus(2, "fault", "unknown", "contradictory")
        if readings["grip"]:
            return GripperStatus(0, "gripping", "stopped", "closed")
        if readings["release"]:
            return GripperStatus(0, "released", "stopped", "open")
        return GripperStatus(1, "unknown", "moving", None)

    def get_status(self) -> GripperStatus:
        """Return current status from configured position sensors."""
        return self.check_sensor_status()

    def grip(self):
        """Command gripper to enter grip state using configured grip output pulse."""
        logger.info("Gripper grip requested")
        self._set_gripper(to_open=False)
        self._wait(1)
        logger.info("Gripper grip completed")

    def release(self):
        """Release gripper from "grip" state using configured release output pulse."""
        logger.info("Gripper release requested")
        self._set_gripper(to_open=True)
        self._wait(1)
        logger.info("Gripper release completed")

def __init__(self, control, config: dict, component_name: str | None = None, sensor_control=None):
    """Initialize gripper from normalized legacy-compatible config.

    Args:
        control: Injected CPX control assembly.
        config: Mapping with ``components.gripper`` and
            ``control_signal_channels``. Optional ``sensor`` config maps
            CPX-E16DI channels 0 and 1 to gripping and release states.
        component_name: Name of gripper component in config, used when multiple grippers are present.
        sensor_control: Optional controller assembly used for sensor module lookup.

    Raises:
        KeyError: Required configuration field is absent.
        ValueError: Configured sensor module cannot be found.
    """
    logger.debug("Gripper initialization started")
    self.control = control
    components = config["components"]
    self.config = components.get("gripper", components.get(component_name))
    if self.config is None and control is None:
        raise KeyError("No instantiated control or valid config given.")
    self.channels_config = self.config["control_signal_channels"]
    self.grip_channel = self.channels_config["grip"]
    self.release_channel = self.channels_config["release"]
    if self.grip_channel == self.release_channel:
        raise ValueError("grip and release channels must be distinct")
    self._owned_control = None
    self._sensor_control = sensor_control
    self.sensor = self._build_sensor(self._sensor_control)
    logger.info(
        "Gripper initialized: grip_channel=%s release_channel=%s sensor=%s",
        self.grip_channel,
        self.release_channel,
        self.sensor is not None,
    )

@classmethod
def from_config(cls, source, component_name: str | None = None, ip_address: str | None = None):
    """Construct gripper and CPX modules from Spec 3.0 configuration."""
    ## TODO: AP module has autorecognition, so explicit IOs are not clear except from some kind of info or other config. Need this to bootstrap and understand system topology of actuators, sensors, etc.
    # TODO: COnfig options: AP still positional in terms of IO modules, this is how the config shuold be structured, avoid hardcoding indices for controls
    # TODO: Map :  cpx.module[index].set_channel(other index) -> human understandable methods/verbs

    adapter = GripperConfigAdapter(source, component_name=component_name)
    config = adapter.get_gripper_config()
    controller = config["components"]["controller"]
    package = ".".join((controller["control_library"], controller["control_system"], controller["control_bus"]))
    selected = config["components"]["gripper"]
    try:
        module_specs = controller["modules"]
        modules = [cls._instantiate_module(package, spec) for spec in module_specs]
        controller_spec = controller["control_module"]
        controller_module, controller_class = cls._single_mapping(controller_spec, "control_module")
        controller_type = getattr(import_module(f"{package}.{controller_module}"), controller_class)
        address = ip_address or os.getenv("GRIPPER_CPX_IP") or controller.get("ip", "192.168.0.2")
        base = controller_type(ip_address=address, modules=modules)
        output_name, output_class = cls._single_mapping(
            selected.get("control_signal_module", {}), "control_signal_module"
        )
        output = next(
            (
                module
                for module in base.modules
                if type(module).__name__ == output_class or getattr(module, "name", None) == output_name
            ),
            None,
        )
        if output is None:
            raise GripperFactoryError(f"Configured output module not found: {output_class}")
        result = cls(output, config, component_name=component_name, sensor_control=base)
        result._owned_control = base
        return result
    except Exception as exc:
        if "base" in locals() and hasattr(base, "shutdown"):
            base.shutdown()
        if isinstance(exc, (ConfigValidationError, GripperFactoryError, ValueError, KeyError)):
            raise
        raise GripperFactoryError(f"Unable to construct configured gripper: {exc}") from exc

class GripperSensor:
    """Read open and closed gripper switches from a digital-input module.

    ``channels["grip"]`` identifies closed/gripping input. ``channels["release"]``
    identifies open/released input. Sensor values are normalized to ``bool``;
    hardware-specific input classes stay behind ``module``.
    """

    def __init__(self, module, channels: dict):
        """Create sensor reader.

        Args:
            module: Digital-input module exposing ``read_channel(channel)``.
            channels: Mapping containing integer ``grip`` and ``release`` channels.
        """
        logger.debug("GripperSensor initialization started")
        self.module = module
        self.grip_channel = channels["grip"]
        self.release_channel = channels["release"]
        logger.debug(
            "GripperSensor initialized: grip_channel=%s release_channel=%s",
            self.grip_channel,
            self.release_channel,
        )

    def read(self) -> dict[str, bool]:
        """Read both configured inputs and map them to semantic states.

        Returns:
            Dictionary with ``grip`` and ``release`` boolean readings.

        Raises:
            Exception: Propagates hardware read failures unchanged.
        """
        logger.debug("GripperSensor read started")
        try:
            readings = {
                "grip": bool(self.module.read_channel(self.grip_channel)),
                "release": bool(self.module.read_channel(self.release_channel)),
            }
        except Exception:
            logger.exception("GripperSensor read failed")
            raise
        logger.debug("Gripper sensor readings: %s", readings)
        return readings

class GripperStatus:
    """Snapshot of gripper position, motion, and fault state.

    ``code`` uses ``0`` for a valid state, ``1`` for indeterminate inputs,
    and ``2`` for contradictory sensor inputs. State strings remain available
    through accessors for callers that do not want to interpret numeric codes.
    """

    def __init__(self, code, gripping_state="unknown", movement_state="unknown", position=None):
        """Create status snapshot.

        Args:
            code: Numeric status code: 0 valid, 1 unknown, 2 fault.
            gripping_state: Semantic gripping state.
            movement_state: Semantic movement state.
            position: ``"gripped"``, ``"released"``, ``"contradictory"``, or ``None``.
        """
        logger.debug(
            "GripperStatus created: code=%s gripping_state=%s movement_state=%s position=%s",
            code,
            gripping_state,
            movement_state,
            position,
        )
        self.code = code
        self.gripping_state = gripping_state
        self.movement_state = movement_state
        self.position = position

    def get_gripping_state(self):
        """Return semantic gripping state."""
        logger.debug("GripperStatus gripping state requested: state=%s", self.gripping_state)
        return self.gripping_state

    def get_movement_state(self):
        """Return semantic movement state."""
        logger.debug("GripperStatus movement state requested: state=%s", self.movement_state)
        return self.movement_state

    def get_position(self):
        """Return semantic position, or ``None`` when unavailable."""
        logger.debug("GripperStatus position requested: position=%s", self.position)
        return self.position
